To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of spatially correlated excitation vectors can improve MSEE performance over fully coherent MIMO channels, and the use of spatial modulation can improve MSEE over partially coherent MIMO channels.
the new techniques outperform existing techniques while requiring substantially less information feedback.

spatial modulation over partially coherent channels is a promising new approach for MIMO communications that is robust to channel coherence and that can be used with a small amount of channel feedback.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of optimal signaling strategies for MIMO channels of unknown and possibly time-varying coherence.
the development of channel excitation strategies for MIMO channels of unknown coherence.
developing new techniques for spatial modulation in MIMO channels of unknown coherence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed spatial modulation strategies are superior to other strategies in terms of mean square error and capacity.
the proposed spatial modulation strategies are optimal in the sense of the MSEE criterion for the MIMO channels considered in the thesis.
the new strategies provide a significant improvement over existing techniques.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed techniques provide a practical and effective solution to the problem of communication over partially coherent MIMO channels.
the new strategies provide a practical alternative to SVD-based channel excitation techniques for MIMO systems.
spatial modulation over partially coherent MIMO channels has a performance that can be characterized by the second-and fourth-moments of the channel transfer matrix.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a mean square estimation approach can be used to develop channel coding strategies for partially coherent MIMO channels that outperform capacity-based approaches.
the MSEE is a more useful metric than the capacity or SINR in the design of MIMO systems.
channel excitation techniques can be devised that minimize the mean square estimation error in an ensemble of channels of arbitrary coherence.
